questions.text: What is the key difference between `T: Draw` and `dyn Draw`?

answers.text: `T: Draw` uses a known concrete type and static dispatch, while `dyn Draw` allows runtime polymorphism
`dyn Draw` is always faster than monomorphization
`T: Draw` allows several different concrete types in one `Vec<T>`
There is no difference between them

questions.explanation: Generics are monomorphized for concrete types, while trait objects hide the concrete type and choose method implementations at runtime.

`Some` always moves the value to another thread
`Option<T>` cannot be destructured

questions.explanation: Ordinary `let` has no branch for a mismatch, so refutable patterns require constructs such as `if let`.

questions.text: How does `_` differ from a name such as `_value` in a pattern? Select all correct answers.

`_value` creates an ordinary binding while suppressing the unused-variable warning
`_value` can participate in ownership moves because it is a binding
`_` always clones the matched value

questions.explanation: A bare `_` ignores the value without binding it, while a leading-underscore name is still a variable and follows ordinary ownership rules.

Disabling type checking
Replacing an enum with a struct

questions.explanation: A match guard adds a logical condition to an arm after the pattern has matched.
